description: On a small brownfield service (ledger-api: Express, Postgres, Redis, Stripe, Docker, GitHub Actions, a Makefile), a non-interactive onboard run writes docs/architecture/overview.md with the nine prescribed sections, the exact build/test/lint commands copied verbatim (the fixture's are deliberately non-default: `npm run lint:strict`, `npm run test:unit`, `make check`), no command the repository does not have, the real entry points, modules, data stores, integrations (credential variable NAMES, never values), deployment shape, real hotspot files and listed unknowns; and it changes nothing else (no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, no beads, no edits). Limits: the sandbox git history is a single commit, so churn cannot rank the hotspots and the checks test that they are real files, not that the ranking is right; the debt-backlog and CLAUDE.md proposals are interactive and only their absence is checked; idempotent update of an existing overview is not covered. The baseline arm is expected to measure the plugin's conventions (the nine-section layout, verbatim commands, unknowns), since any capable model can describe a small repository. Claude only: Step 1.1 resolves toolchain-cli through the tool-path-resolution tiers, which fail on Pi in a sandbox without an installed bundle.
prompt:
I am new to this codebase. Get me oriented on it and save the result under docs/architecture/. --foreman

This is a non-interactive run: ask no questions, choose the recommended option for anything unclear, and answer no to every follow-up proposal (do not touch CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, create no beads). Change nothing in the repository except that one document.

checks.command: node '{{repo}}/evals/checks/ensemble-onboard.js' overview-commands --commands 'make check,npm run lint:strict,npm run test:unit,npm run build'
